facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Pucapristis.
The type species of the genus is Pucapristis branisi.
The genus was described by Schaeffer in 1963.
Fossils of Pucapristis first appear in rocks dating from the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: fossils first appear in the fossil record in rocks dating from the Maastrichtian stage

facts.statement: The Maastrichtian stage marks the final portion of the Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: the Maastrichtian is the final portion of the Cretaceous Period

facts.statement: Pucapristis lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Pucapristis is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The parent group of Pucapristis is the family Sclerorhynchidae.
The El Molino Formation in Bolivia produces Pucapristis tooth fossils in abundance.
facts.quote: The El Molino Formation of Bolivia produces Pucapristis tooth fossils in abundance

facts.statement: Remains of Pucapristis can be excavated from the Yacoraite Formation in Salta Province, northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: The Yacoraite Formation of Salta Province in northwestern Argentina is another locality from which Pucapristis remains can be excavated
